results.summary: This project implements a simple full adder with three inputs and two outputs. It is intended to be tested by running all eight possible input combinations. No external hardware is required. The documentation is minimal and the design is a basic educational exercise.

This design controls the segments of a 7-segment display, including the decimal point, based on input signals. It was created as part of an IEEE-sponsored Tiny Tapeout workshop in San Diego in November 2024, in collaboration with UCSD. The design is tested by toggling the inputs and observing the segments turn on and off. It requires an external 7-segment display for output.

This project is a 2-bit adder that adds two inputs and outputs the result to two LEDs. It is tested by inputting two numbers and verifying the output is correct. External hardware required includes a DIP switch for input and two LEDs for output. The documentation is brief and the design is a basic educational exercise.

This design implements four half adders, each adding two one-bit integers and producing four outputs for an LED display. It is a basic educational project. No external hardware is required. The documentation is minimal and does not describe testing.

This project aims to control a 7-segment display using mixed logic gates, but the functionality is not yet fully defined. The documentation states that the gates make signals do funky things and that testing is to be determined. External hardware includes a 7-segment display, input board, output board, and switch panel. The design is a work in progress and lacks clear specifications.

This project is a BCD decoder that displays a 0 on a 7-segment display when pin 1 is off. It is tested by plugging it in and observing the display. No external hardware is required. The documentation is very limited and the design appears to be incomplete or not fully functional.

This design uses a multiplexer to control an LED and a display module based on input signals. It is tested by toggling input 7 and inputs 4 and 6 to observe the lighting behavior. External hardware includes an LED display and an LED diode. The documentation is brief but provides enough information to understand the basic operation.

This design flashes the letter E on a 7-segment display when switch pins 1 and 7 are powered and the clock is on. It is tested by powering those pins and the clock. External hardware requires either a 7-segment display or LEDs connected to the outputs. The design uses a 2 Hz clock and is a simple educational project.

This project is an 8x3 encoder, which converts eight input lines into a three-bit binary output. The documentation states that testing and external hardware are works in progress. No further details are provided. The design is likely a basic educational exercise.

This design uses NOT and AND gates to display the letter J on a 7-segment display when the code 6531 is entered. It is tested by entering that code and observing the display. External hardware requires a single-digit 7-segment display. The project is a simple educational exercise.
